abstract:
Coding sequence design requires optimizing multiple biological properties, which may be either aligned or in trade-off, and are typically measured as continuous-valued metrics. However, existing codon design methods lack explicit control over these objectives. Moreover, current controllable generation techniques are largely developed for discrete, human-interpretable attributes, leaving a gap in controllably steering continuous biological properties in genomic sequence design.
We introduce ARCADE (Activation engineeRing for ControllAble coDon dEsign), a machine learning framework for flexible and controllable multi-objective codon design. ARCADE leverages pretrained genomic language models and extends activation engineering from discrete attribute control to continuous-valued biological metrics. By deriving biologically meaningful semantic steering vectors in the model's activation space, ARCADE enables direct control over properties such as Codon Adaptation Index, minimum free energy, GC content, as well as their combinations. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that ARCADE supports robust single- and multi-objective steering, enabling simultaneous modulation of multiple properties without retraining model parameters.
Source code for the method and to reproduce the results is available at https://github.com/Kingsford-Group/arcade and archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21140668).
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
